app/static/index.html — the single static page

Purpose

The entire web UI's markup: one page, no framework, no build step, no CDN. It defines the DOM contract that app.js consumes — every id the script reaches for — and the visible structure: header (with the log viewer), the fetch form, the error banner, the result section (transcript panel + summary panel), and the saved-transcripts section.

Public surface

The asset set is exactly three files referenced with absolute paths: /style.css, /app.js, and this page (served by the static mount at /). The effective API is the id/class contract with app.js:

  • Fetch flow: url-input, fetch-form, fetch-btn, fetch-spinner, fetch-label.
  • Result: error-banner, result, video-title, video-language, transcript-panel, copy-btn, download-btn.
  • Summarization: provider-picker, summarize-btn, summarize-spinner, summary-panel, summary-text, summary-copy-btn.
  • Saved list: saved-list, saved-empty, saved-count, saved-refresh-btn.
  • Log viewer: logs-toggle, log-panel.

Invariants

  • No build step, no framework, no CDN. The file is hand-maintained markup; anything requiring a transpiler or a third-party script is off-limits for this app.
  • The hidden attribute is the visibility contract, and the CSS rule [hidden] { display: none !important; } in style.css keeps it authoritative even for styled elements. app.js toggles only hidden.
  • The log panel lives in the header, as the header's second row — not at the bottom of the page flow — so opening it never requires scrolling. The header is a column of rows (titles + toggle on the first row, panel on the second), with row gap providing the spacing.
  • Accessibility is structural, not script-added: role="alert" on the error banner, aria-labels on the input, panels, and provider picker, tabindex="0" on the scrollable <pre> panels, type="button" on non-submit buttons, aria-hidden on the spinners.
  • Buttons start disabled where app.js requires it (copy, download, summarize, the provider picker); the script enables them as state allows.
  • The result section is hidden until the first transcript — fresh fetch and saved-row display both render into this same single panel.

Log events emitted

None (markup). The log-panel <pre> is where app.js appends the humanized server log lines.

Error codes raised/handled

None (markup). The error-banner element is where app.js surfaces them.

Design decisions

Resolved from the archived change design docs:

  • 2026-10-29-youtube-transcript D6 — one static page served by FastAPI's StaticFiles; no framework, no bundler, no CDN.
  • 2026-11-02-add-saved-transcript-list decision 6 — the saved section below #result: header over a bounded, scrollable <ul>, rows as keyboard-accessible <button>s.
  • 2026-11-03-add-log-viewer decision 6 — the #logs-toggle button and the #log-panel <pre> (monospace, scrollable, bounded max-height).
  • 2026-11-06-move-log-panel-into-header D1–D3 — push-down placement in the header (normal document flow, not an overlay), the column-of-rows header with align-items: stretch, and row-gap spacing replacing the old margin-top while the panel keeps its max-height: 40vh internal scroll.
